summary.intent: Execute all 8 plans in Phase 60 (IPNS Verification Cross-Layer Closeout) using the GSD wave-based parallel execution workflow, then run the full ship-phase loop (verify → secure → simplify → SDK E2E → CodeRabbit → ship → CI).
summary.outcome: All 8 plans executed (7 code-complete, 60-08 paused at human-action staging cutover checkpoint); a ship-blocking regression introduced by 60-05 was caught by the SDK E2E gate and fixed; security audit returned 27/27 threats closed; 7 additional CodeRabbit findings fixed; 3 final TS commits were still being written when the transcript ended.

repo: Ed25519 IPNS records do NOT embed pubKey in the record protobuf — it lives in the name (k51…). The DB `publicKey` column was the authoritative source; 60-05 deleted the enrich that supplied it, causing the strict client to throw `fail closed` on every resolve.
The `gsd-tools` commit helper reports `commit_failed` (lint-staged stderr) even when the commit actually lands — always verify with `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry.
`cargo fmt --check` reports drift across the whole workspace due to a local rustfmt version mismatch vs repo; never run blanket `cargo fmt` — executor commits pass CI as-is.
lint-staged does not process `.rs` files, only TS/JSON/MD — Rust commits land without fmt hooks.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL) — patch PR bodies via `gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.
`git push` / `git fetch` are blocked in the sandbox environment — must run with sandbox disabled.

The 1Password SSH signing agent wedges after many rapid commits (`op-ssh-sign: failed to fill whole buffer`) — requires quit-and-reopen of the 1Password desktop app; keys still listed by the agent but signing requests fail.
CodeRabbit bundles nitpick findings in the review body AND as inline review threads — both must be fetched and resolved separately.

IPNS unit tests in `ipns.service.spec.ts` mocked `parseIpnsRecord` to include `pubKey` (unrealistic for Ed25519), which is why the 60-05 regression passed all 343 unit tests but failed 28/89 SDK E2E tests.

code.finding: resolveRecord on equal-sequence returned the bare network result (no sig fields) instead of the DB cached record. The removed `withCachedPublicKey` and equal-seq enrich were load-bearing — they supplied pubKey from the DB `publicKey` column, which parseIpnsRecordBytes does not extract for Ed25519 records.

parseCachedRecord must supply pubKey from the validated DB `publicKey` column and fail-closed when that column is absent — publish already enforces deriveIpnsName(publicKey) === ipnsName, and the client re-checks the binding.

TS resolve path skipped the EOL block entirely when Validity was not a Uint8Array (absent field), while Rust fail-closes via .ok_or_else(). Fixed to throw on absent Validity, matching D-07 cross-layer contract.

decode_ipns_cbor_validity returned on first-wins for duplicate 'Validity' keys (early return), while its sibling decode_ipns_cbor_data rejects duplicates with an explicit guard. A maliciously crafted record with two Validity entries decoded ambiguously across parsers — now hardened to reject duplicates.

register_device swallowed ALL errors from fetch_and_decrypt_registry with `Err(_) => None`, treating verification failures (VerifyError::Invalid) as legitimate first-device bootstrap. Fixed to only bootstrap on ApiError::IpnsNotFound (HTTP 404); all other errors propagate.

parse_rfc3339_to_unix_secs was lenient: trailing components accepted silently, and impossible dates (2026-02-31) were not rejected — the Hinnant civil_from_days algorithm rolls them into the following month, extending expiry. Fixed with trailing-component check and leap-aware day-of-month validation.
The short-TTL verify cache was unbounded — fixed with MAX_CACHE_SIZE eviction to prevent unbounded memory growth.
Web vault-settings sequence-fallback swallowed verification failures; resolveIpnsRecord returns null only for true not-found — other errors (verification failure) must propagate fail-closed.

The 60-05 D-06 unit test codified the buggy behavior by asserting signatureV2/data are undefined on equal-seq, and mocked parseIpnsRecord to include pubKey (unrealistic for Ed25519 records). Both issues masked the regression — test updated to assert corrected strict-verifiable behavior.

workflow: The SDK E2E gate (`pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-e2e test`) is the only suite that exercises the real client→API IPNS publish/resolve round-trip; unit suites mock the resolve boundary and miss integration regressions — this gate caught the 60-05 regression that 343 unit tests missed.

Sequential gsd-executor subagents on the feature branch (not worktree isolation) is the safer approach for security-critical phases with tight cross-plan dependencies — avoids worktree merge conflicts at the cost of wall-clock time.

Adversarial triage workflows for CodeRabbit findings (parallel subagents with distinct skeptic prompts) are effective at separating real in-scope fixes from false positives — 4/15 findings were false positives including the pre-increment-sequence findings.

The short-circuit rule in secure-phase (`threats_open: 0 AND register_authored_at_plan_time: true`) skips the auditor and goes directly to SECURITY.md write — only valid when all threats were planned upfront and all plans have summaries.

When a background Bash command is cut off before all chained commands complete, the partial state must be explicitly checked rather than assumed (the 3 TS commits were still pending when the transcript ended).
Grouping fix commits by owning plan (e.g., `fix(60-05): restore ...`) rather than one mega-commit makes the security audit trail and git blame more useful for future investigators.

friction: 1Password SSH signing agent wedged mid-session after ~28 rapid commits, requiring user intervention to restart the app before any further commits could land.
The `gsd-tools` commit helper emits `commit_failed` (lint-staged normal output) even on success — created repeated false alarms and verification loops across the session.
`git push`/`git fetch` blocked in sandbox requires a context switch to unsandboxed execution for every push.
Background Bash process was cut off before completing all 5 chained commit commands, leaving 3 TS fix commits unwritten.

The `cargo fmt --check` workspace-wide drift created confusion about whether edits introduced formatting violations — needed explicit investigation to confirm it was a version mismatch, not real drift.
CodeRabbit CLI returned 15 findings requiring a full adversarial triage workflow (15 subagents) to classify — significant overhead before ship.
The worktree merge protocol is unsupported for worktree-isolated agents in the GSD harness, forcing fallback to sequential execution and higher wall-clock time.
